messages.author: 05e878158bf32998
messages.subject: Progress bar for parallelized HMC
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am running three HMC chains in parallel using parLapply() with the nimbleHMC functions in a workflow similar to this one: https://r-nimble.org/nimbleExamples/parallelizing_NIMBLE.html

However, with a reasonable number of iterations, computation time is still tremendous due to the complexity of my model. I would thus like to have a progress bar displayed while the HMC chains run in parallel. Alternatively, an a priori calculation of the approximate total computation time would be a good start.

I have tried several things, such as replacing parLapply() with pblapply() from the pbapply package or future_lapply() from the future.apply package, which would display a progress bar, but that one is useless, as it just jumps from 0% to 100% at once, when the operation has finished.

Did anyone come up with a good way of getting a progress bar while running MCMC (or HMC) chains in parallel?


Cheers,

Leander

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Progress bar for parallelized HMC
parts:
Hi Leander,

Without investigating how to pass output from the parallel workers back to the main R session, I think the easiest path will be an a priori calculation of total computation time.

Once the HMC warmup period is over, the computation time should scale roughly linearly with the number of iterations unless the chain gets "stuck" for periods of time in certain problematic parts of the space in which the NUTS sampler tree depths are large.  So if you have an idea of a sufficient warmup length, you could do something like the following to get an estimate:

Suppose the warmup length is 500.

1) Run a chain for 500 total iterations (including warmup) with a warmup of 500 to be able to time just the warmup.
2) Run a separate chain for 1500 total iterations with a warmup of 500.
3) Subtract the times and divide by 1000 to estimate the time per iteration after warmup.

-chris
